updates.note: Declined to comment on any link between the AIS anomaly and the blast: 'We are not going to discuss matters under investigation... Our focus is the safety of the waterway.'

Told Gulfwater the spoofed identity's track sat near the entrance channel two weeks before the blast; 'The data tells you where a signal was. It does not tell you who sent it or why'; cautioned against 'drawing a straight line.'

Heard the blast from home around 1 a.m.: 'It wasn't thunder. I know thunder... one big thump, and then every dog on the island started in'; still selling hooks and ice from a folding table in the gutted shop; 'I sell bait, not theories.'

Arc beat (hospital interview, by phone Tues., Nov. 2): recovering from a broken arm and concussion; remembers the sound, 'then I was looking at the sky'; 'Cap got us home'; plans to return to work, 'Not this week. But I'm going back.'

Described the blast: came off the port bow, 'the boat lifted, and the water came up over the rail'; counted heads, all accounted for 'in under a minute'; declined to discuss tug damage; won't speculate on cause ('I drive a tugboat'); visits Fontenot most days.
'Our soldiers and their equipment are ready to go. We'll move when the port is ready, and not before'; declined to discuss timelines or staging.
Would not describe methods or equipment; 'Our teams will search every yard of that channel they need to... we are not going to put a date on it. When we say it is clear, we want it to be clear.'
'There isn't a second door at this scale'; market question shifted 'from damage to duration'; no number is 'the right answer for safety' but 'a hard answer for a cargo schedule.'
Port ready to work 'around the clock' once the channel reopens; 'nothing moves in or out until the Coast Guard says it is safe'; 'We would rather open a day late than open wrong.'

Recalled Gulf Provider's month-late berthing: 'the cargo can be ready and the water can still say no'; customers call every morning for a date he doesn't have; some shippers asking about trucking from other ports.

Bays closed by oil and the pass closed by the blast: 'Where do I go? You tell me where, I go tomorrow'; trip notebook since mid-September reads 'no trip'; still owes on the boat and fuel dock, deckhand has two kids; hasn't sought other work because no one gives a timeline.
Power steady since last month's backup generator failure; cause still under review; 'base services are operating... We'll share what we can when the review is complete.'
Depot back at full production; credited DLA Distribution Corpus Christi parts support; praised workforce that 'came back every time' and families who 'carried a lot.'

ER visits in low-income bayside neighborhoods still about 40% above normal: 'When one part of the county recovers and another part doesn't, that tells us something'; urged early clinic visits, med lists, gloves and masks for flood cleanup; 'For some families, the recovery started a lot later than that.'

People delay care because 'the doctor is two buses away'; says she has driven more people to the ER this fall than in the last five years; many families still in damp rentals: 'You can't separate the house from the health.'
Channel stays closed: 'will reopen when the search is complete and the Captain of the Port is satisfied it is safe... We are not giving a date today.'

Arc beat (second device): 'Navy teams located a second explosive device near the entrance channel and rendered it safe. No one was injured. The search... will continue until we are confident it is complete'; would not describe the device or exact location.
Repeated to national wire that no one was injured and the search continues; declined to describe the device.
On the second device: 'We can confirm we are investigating... We are not going to discuss evidence.'
On the second device: markets 'were hoping for a date. Today they got a reason it isn't coming yet.'

To Gulfwater: 'A second find does not shorten the process. It confirms why we follow it'; reopening notice will go to mariners through the usual channels; again declined comment on any link to the AIS anomaly.
To Gulfwater: teams continue working with the Coast Guard; declined to describe the device or its position.

After the second device: 'We knew the search would take what it takes... The brigade is ready. When the port is ready, we go'; declined schedule, staging, destination; movement will be announced publicly ('Nobody's going to hear it from a rumor first').
Re-quoted: no one injured Friday, search continues; would not describe the device.

'In September, the water took the buildings. Now it's taking the customers'; summer was 'real good'; second device rattled the island more than the first; praised the Navy crews on the water; keeping the folding table open weekends, 'Directions are still free' (callback to his summer joke).
Twelfth day of halt: 'Last week, buyers were waiting. This week, they're planning around it'; some business 'may not come straight back'; local storage absorbing crude but 'Tanks fill.'

Profile, eight weeks on: a bucket in her hallway catches a roof leak since September; back bedroom smells of mildew, moved her youngest (6) into her own room; landlord says 'soon' ('my least favorite word'); still rides two buses to clients; 'Who takes care of the people who take care of people?'; wants to hear where to sign up for aid before 'my neighbor's cousin.' (Bucket not yet named.)
'Everybody on my street is waiting on something: a landlord, an adjuster, a ride, a phone call back'; promises to knock on doors the day federal aid details are known.
No change in port condition; Captain of the Port will reopen when the search is complete; 'we ask operators not to plan on rumor.'
Port working with the Coast Guard and pilots on a restart plan; won't say when ('that isn't our call'); 'Berths are clear, terminals are staffed, and the plan for the first days is written.'
Explained reopening authority: Captain of the Port decides; 'That decision rests on what the teams in the water tell us.'
Re-quoted in Ledger explainer: 'When we say it is clear, we want it to be clear.'
Announced reopening: 'The search is complete, and the Captain of the Port has reopened the Corpus Christi Ship Channel to vessel traffic'; thanked Navy teams and port partners.
'The channel has been cleared. Our teams covered every stretch of water they needed to, and they are proud to hand it back to the port.'

Reopening day: 'This is a good day for the Port of Corpus Christi'; channel open from the jetties to the Inner Harbor; working around the clock; would not estimate backlog clearance ('We'll go as fast as safety allows. Faster than that, we don't go').
'First good morning I've had since October'; called three customers before 8 a.m. to say 'moving'; won't promise arrival dates anymore ('I've learned').

On reopening: 'The door is open. Now comes the line'; expects 'a catch-up period, not a snap back'; 'Markets have short memories for weather and longer ones for security'; buyers want to know the channel 'was cleared, not just opened.'
Veterans Day: base services normal; generator failure review continues; 'people kept showing up for work and for each other. That's a good thing to remember on Veterans Day.'
Arc beat (military outload proceeds): port loading the brigade and tankers at the same time a day after reopening; 'this is what that means' to be a strategic military seaport.

Arc beat (brigade sails): 'Loading is under way... Today we get to do the job'; equipment sails over the next five days; destination only 'an overseas rotation'; declined ship, route, aircraft numbers; 'We go when we can go. We're going now.'
Traffic 'moving safely and in order'; asked operators for patience; 'The order of movements is set for safety, not for any one customer.'
Post-reopening AIS 'looks like a port getting back to work'; mid-October questions 'still open, and public data alone isn't going to close them.'

Watched the ships from a lawn chair on the beach road ('Best seat on the island... Free, too'); 'the pass being open means the people come back. That's how this town works'; still selling from the folding table.
Mentioned only: still recovering; called his captain to ask if the channel was open.

Watched ships pass the jetties the day after reopening: 'Two weeks ago I was out there counting heads. Today I'm standing here counting ships'; Fontenot called to ask if it was open; will return to the water 'when the company has a boat for him'; 'I'll watch the water at the jetties like I always have. Harder, maybe.'

Arc beat (registration opens): 'Register even if you're not sure you qualify'; file with insurance too, keep receipts; FEMA never charges and staff never ask for money; 'If someone calls you offering to speed up your application for a fee, hang up.'
'We know the lines are long... Nobody loses their place by registering online or by phone instead. If you can't stand in a line, you don't have to.'

Registered for FEMA aid Saturday, Nov. 13, at a recovery center after leaving at 6:10 a.m. on two buses; registered a little after noon; brought ID, kids' papers, lease, bank card and a photo of her ceiling; 'I've been getting a call since September'; a neighbor watched her kids.
In line with a clipboard and cooler; drove three car-less neighbors to register; 'Same list, new column'; wants to retire the clipboard someday.
'There's no advantage to standing in line. We want every eligible household registered.'

Fellowship hall became a registration help desk (two borrowed laptops, charger strip, sign 'FEMA help here. Bring your papers.'); volunteers wrote registration numbers on index cards; 'Most of them can't get to a center'; 'I'm not going to call it a good day until the help actually shows up.'
Monitoring 'doesn't mean anybody walks away'; crews still checking shorelines and marshes; urged people who see oil to call the hotline.

Showed where the oil line was on North Beach; beach 'forgets faster than people do'; throat raw for a week; a neighbor's grandson had a rash; asks who pays doctor bills; wants agencies to say 'what they can claim, where to file, and who signs the check.'
Backlog 'getting shorter every day'; 'I've learned not to promise the water anything. But we're close to a normal week'; declined to discuss the military movement beyond the Army's statement.

Held shipments arriving after reopening; a customer sent him a photo of building-supply pallets ('I saved it'); 'Twice this fall the cargo was ready and the water wasn't'; wants a plan B not dependent on the channel.
Speaking generally: renters can show occupancy with utility bills, pay stubs, school or employer letters, bank statements; respond quickly and call the helpline if unsure.

Arc beat (aid application stalls): two days after registering, FEMA asked for proof of occupancy; her lease is a one-page landlord-written form with her name misspelled; landlord unreachable except to say repairs 'soon'; uploaded a school letter for her youngest showing her address; 'I'm very good at waiting. I should get paid for it.'
Volunteers helped Rosa find and photograph a school letter; 'The people with the least paperwork are the people who need the help the most'; expects many renters on her list to hit the same snag.

Claims process opens: 'If the spill cost you income or damaged your property, file'; start the claim and keep adding receipts, trip logs, tax records, photos; no date for fishing reopening; 'You don't need to pay anybody to start a claim.'
On claims opening: 'Finally, somebody wants to see my notebook... Years of notebooks'; planned to file within days; 'Paper doesn't fish. But paper is what I have.'
Re-quoted from Sunday asking 'what people can claim, where to file, and who signs the check.'
'Start the claim, then keep adding to it. Nobody expects you to have it all on day one.'

Checked her FEMA account three times at the hub on Wed., Nov. 17: deposit details unchanged ('still my little account'); will check daily 'like the weather'; application still waiting on FEMA to accept her school letter; 'Now I need proof that my money lives in my account.'

Volunteers helped neighbors log in on two borrowed laptops; says a couple of people found account numbers they didn't recognize (unverified); 'the people with the least are going to lose the most'; wrote FEMA's helpline on her needs whiteboard.
Base services normal; 'a good neighbor and a charged phone go a long way' for neighbors needing help with aid applications.
To the base weekly: military households can register like any other; 'register, even if you're not sure you qualify.'
Re-quoted: start with what you have and add documents; no date yet for reopening the bays.

Arc beat (files spill damage claim, Thu., Nov. 18): brought eleven spiral notebooks, rubber-banded fuel receipts and boat papers in a grocery bag; father taught him to write it down ('someday somebody will ask'); pass open but bays closed ('One door opens, the other stays shut'); deckhand picking up day work; 'Tell me when I can fish.' New detail: eleven notebooks.

Confirmed (Fri., Nov. 19): 'We have confirmed unauthorized access to some applicant accounts. We are urging every applicant to log in and verify their direct-deposit information today'; no numbers, method or payment details given; FEMA never asks for passwords or fees.
Statement to the Ledger; when asked how many, how, when, or whether payments were diverted, said FEMA would release more when it could.
Deposit details still correct Friday morning; 'I'm checking it like my kids check the fridge. Every hour, for no reason, just in case.'
'My neighbors told me Wednesday. FEMA told us Friday... Now tell people how they get their money if it went to the wrong place.'
Same confirmation to the national wire; FEMA will share more when it can.

On FEMA's confirmation: 'Until the agency says how the accounts were accessed, anyone who tells you exactly what happened is guessing'; advice: check deposit info, unique password, extra sign-in protection; 'Speed is the point of disaster aid. It's also what makes it a target.' No attribution.
Arc beat (account security warning): 'Verify your information now, even if you checked last week. FEMA will never call, text or email you to ask for your password. If someone does, it isn't us.'
Checks her account on the bus between clients; info unchanged; application still pending on the school letter; 'Now I'm guarding money I don't have yet. That's a new kind of tired.'
Whiteboard now reads 'CHECK YOUR DEPOSIT. EVERY DAY.' in red; 'My people don't have a cushion. A week late is a late fee'; hall's laptops stay out through Thanksgiving week.
Short quote: 'If it isn't us, hang up and call us.'

Pre-Thanksgiving advice: damp or leaking homes 'can keep affecting health for months'; dry and clean mildew with gloves and mask; tell your doctor about stress and sleep problems; 'Hand-washing is still the cheapest medicine we have.'
'We still see people who put off care until they couldn't anymore'; urged bringing a med list or photos; 'We'll be here Thursday. I'd just rather see you Tuesday at a clinic.' No patient specifics.

Thanksgiving week: checks her FEMA deposit details on the 6:10 a.m. bus every morning ('good morning, little account'); application still pending on the school letter; hallway leak still in a bucket; youngest (6) asking about turkey; 'Next year I want to be thankful for a ceiling.'

Planning Thanksgiving dinner at the fellowship hall for anyone (turkeys from members, tamales from a neighbor, pies from a bakery); laptops on a side table with sign 'Check your deposit before dessert'; 'So we'll eat, and we'll check'; families 'guarding an account like it's a front porch.'

Eleven days after reopening: 'the queue first, then the tanks'; rebooked cargoes don't swing back at once; the fall 'added something buyers hadn't really priced at this port before'; expects near-normal volumes by early December, 'a forecast, not a promise.'
